issues.reason: Kernel body-size middleware and MCP transport guards expose different rejection envelopes; identify the governing layer.
issues.body_evidence_excerpt:
## Gap

`BodySizeLimitMiddleware` runs at priority 70, ahead of every controller and therefore ahead of `StreamableHttpTransportGuard`. For three request shapes it answers first with an oversize refusal where the guard would have refused differently — or, in one case, would not have refused at all.

Surfaced while verifying #2594. **None of these reproduces that issue's defect** — the envelope is JSON-RPC in every case, which is what #2594 was about. They are precedence differences, filed so they are recorded rather than rediscovered.

## The three cases

Verified by reading `BodySizeLimitMiddleware::process()` against `StreamableHttpTransportGuard::validate()`.

| # | Request | Answered | Guard would answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Oversize POST from a disallowed `Origin` | `413` / `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` | `403` / `FORBIDDEN_ORIGIN` |
| 2 | `GET /mcp` with an oversize `Content-Length` | `413` / `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` | never size-checks GET at all |
